blurb: Shang and Zhou religion: divination, veneration of royal ancestors, and the high god Di (later Tian, Heaven) — the sacred order behind the human one.

events.description: Divination records carved on ox bones and turtle shells at Anyang — the earliest Chinese writing. Shang kings queried ancestors and high gods about harvests, warfare, and ritual.
events.title: Oracle-bone inscriptions

events.description: A divination manual of 64 hexagrams with judgments and line statements, built up during the Western Zhou and later expanded into a cosmology of change.
events.title: Yijing (I Ching / Book of Changes)

events.description: 305 poems from the early Zhou — folk songs, court odes, and temple hymns including sacrificial odes to royal ancestors. Became one of the Confucian Five Classics.
events.title: Shijing (Classic of Poetry)

name: Ancient Chinese folk religion
